_notes: Augustinian formation, third pool: the theology years to solemn profession, diaconate, the pastoral year, and ordination. E3 §12, §14.

events.title: The Thesis on the Founder
events.body: The union asks a thesis of its licentiate students and the Augustinians are expected, by everyone, to write on Augustine, and the Franciscan who directs theses has said that he would like to see one Augustinian in his career write on someone else, and has looked at you. {@confrere} is writing on the Confessions. The formation director has said the choice is yours and that the province reads titles.

choices.label: Augustine, on friendship, since that is the order
choices.outcome: The Franciscan sighs and directs it well. It is a good thesis and the province is pleased and the formation director says that it is the first thesis on friendship the province has had, which is odd, given the order, and it is read by the novice directors for twenty years.

choices.label: Someone else; the Franciscan is right
choices.outcome: It is on a Servite mystic nobody in the order has read and it is good and the province is puzzled, and the Franciscan is delighted and says it is the first Augustinian thesis he has enjoyed directing, and the Servites send you a letter, and the formation director says the title was brave.

choices.label: Augustine's sermons to his people, since you are for the parishes
choices.outcome: The Franciscan says it is a pastoral topic and directs it anyway, and it is the thesis you use, since the sermons are the sermons, and the province's pastors, hearing of it, ask for a copy, and it is the only thesis of your class that is read by a pastor.

events.title: The Prefect of the Hall
events.body: The house has asked a student brother to be prefect of the student hall, which means the rota, the noise, and the men who are late for the Office, and the formation director has said it is you, since you are the one the others listen to, which is not the same as the one they like, and asked whether you would rather he had chosen the other thing.

choices.label: Take it, and keep the rota and not the men
choices.outcome: The rota is kept and the men are not, and the hall is orderly and cold for a year, and the formation director says at the renewal that you were a good prefect and asks whether you enjoyed it, and you say no, and he says good.

choices.label: Take it, and keep the men and let the rota slip
choices.outcome: The hall is warm and late for the Office, and the prior says so, and the formation director says the Augustinian answer is both, and that you have found half of it, and that the other half is the prior's, and you find it in the second term.

choices.label: Ask him to choose the one they like
choices.outcome: He does. The one they like is a bad prefect and a loved one and the hall is a mess and happy, and the formation director says at the end of the year that he should have insisted, and that you should have let him, and you both learn something.

events.title: The Friend Who Is Failing
events.body: {@confrere} is failing. Not the studies, which are fine, but the thing the community votes on, which is the life: he is out of the house more than in it, has a friend outside it nobody has met, and is, the house says at recreation when he is not there, not one of us this year. The renewal is in April and the house will vote, and he has not asked you for anything, and you are his friend.

choices.label: Ask him, straight, what is happening
choices.outcome: He tells you: the friend outside is a woman, and it is not what the house thinks, and it is not nothing, and he does not know what it is, and has not known how to say it, and is glad you asked. He tells the formation director the next day, himself, and the house votes, and it is close, and he renews, and it holds.

choices.label: Tell the formation director you are worried
choices.outcome: The director says he knows and has been waiting for the friend to come, and that he had hoped it would be you who sent him, and you say you will try, and try, and the friend comes in a week, and does not know it was you, and it was.

choices.label: Wait; a friend does not investigate a friend
choices.outcome: You wait. The house votes and it does not carry, and he leaves in May, and is a good man in the world, and says to you at a wedding, years on, that he had wanted someone to ask, and you had been the someone, and it is a thing you carry.

events.title: The First Homily
events.body: The union sends its fourth-year students to preach at the friars' Masses, once, under a professor who listens from the sacristy, and the professor is a Servite who says the Augustinians preach as if the congregation had read the Confessions, which it has not. Yours is the Sunday nine o'clock in the parish the priory runs, three hundred people, a Gospel about the lost sheep, and eight minutes.

choices.label: Preach it from the Confessions, since that is the sheep
choices.outcome: The Servite says afterward that it was beautiful and that thirty people understood it, and that the other two hundred and seventy are the parish, and that you should preach to them next time, and you do, and the thirty come anyway.

choices.label: Preach it to the parish: one sheep, one shepherd, four minutes
choices.outcome: The Servite says nothing in the sacristy and then says, at lunch, that it was the first Augustinian homily he has heard that a farmer could have followed, and that the founder preached like that, and the Augustinians have forgotten, and you have not.

choices.label: Tell them a story about a sheep, and say nothing else
choices.outcome: The story is a good one and the parish laughs in the right place and is quiet in the right place, and the Servite says it was a homily with the theology hidden, which is the hardest kind, and asks whether it was on purpose, and you are not sure.

events.title: The Year of the Point of No Return
events.body: The fifth year begins and ends with solemn profession and the formation director has said, at the first meeting, that this is the year to leave if you are going to, since after it there is no leaving that is not a breaking, and that he says it every year to every fifth-year man and that some of them have thanked him for it, later, from the world. He has asked whether there is anything you would like to say, now, in September.

choices.label: Say no, and mean it
choices.outcome: He nods and says he believed you, which he does not always, and the year is the year: the studies, the house, the vote, and the day, and the day is the day, and you are professed with your hands steady, for once.

choices.label: Say there is something, and say it
choices.outcome: It is a thing you had not said to anyone and it takes an hour and he listens and says it is the kind of thing the year is for, and that you should carry it to the day and see if it is still there, and it is, and it is smaller, and you profess with it, which is what the order does.

choices.label: Say you will tell him in Lent
choices.outcome: He says Lent is late and that he will hold you to it, and does, and in Lent it is a different thing than it would have been in September, since a year has passed, and it is easier, and he says you should have said the September thing, and you had not known what it was.

events.title: Speaking Before the Vote
events.body: The community meets before the solemn vote and the man being voted on is not in the room, which is the custom, and this year the formation director has asked whether you would like to speak to the house before you leave it, which is not the custom and is allowed, and the house is looking at you, and {@old_friar} has nodded, once, which means yes.

choices.label: Speak: what the house has been to you, in a minute
choices.outcome: It is a minute and the house is quiet after it and the vote is not close. The old friar says afterward that nobody had done it in his time and that it should be done, and the formation director does it with every fifth-year man after, and calls it the minute.

choices.label: Thank them, and go
choices.outcome: It is enough. The vote carries. The old friar says the thank-you was the right length and that a speech would have been a campaign, and the formation director does not ask the next man, and you are not sure which of you was right.

choices.label: Say the house knows you, and go
choices.outcome: It does. The vote carries. One friar says at recreation that it was a little cold, and the old friar says it was Augustinian, and the two of them argue about it, which is the house at its best.

events.title: The Man From the Mission
events.body: The mission superior is home for the chapter and has come to the studium, as he does, to look at the fifth-year men, since the mission takes one every few years and he chooses. He has sat with you at supper and talked about the mountain for an hour, and then said that he would like to know whether you would go if sent, and that he will not ask again, and that he will remember the answer.

choices.label: Say yes
choices.outcome: He nods and says nothing more. Three years after ordination the letter comes, and it is the mountain, and you go, and it is the life, or the first half of it, and he is there for the first year and then is not, since he dies on the mountain, and you bury him, and it is your mission then.

choices.label: Say no, and why
choices.outcome: He listens to the why and says it is a good reason and that the mission has taken men with worse ones, and does not ask again, and the letter does not come, and you are in the parishes, and hear of the mountain from the men who went, and are glad of them.

choices.label: Ask him what the mountain did to him
choices.outcome: He tells you, for the rest of supper and into recreation: thirty years, a language, a people, and a body that will not last, and a happiness he does not have a word for in English, and you say yes then, since he has said it, and he remembers.

events.title: Solemn Profession
events.body: The day. The provincial receives the vows, and the formula is the same words as three Septembers and means, now, the thing it said, and the house is in the choir and the family is in the nave and {@confrere} is beside you, since you profess together, and it is the first time in five years that you have both been sure of the same thing at the same time.

choices.label: Say the formula together, as the constitutions allow
choices.outcome: The two voices are one, mostly. The provincial says afterward that he has received a hundred professions and that the double ones are the ones he remembers, and the house says it was like a wedding, which was not what anyone meant and was true.

choices.label: Say it alone, each of you, since a vow is one man's
choices.outcome: The provincial receives them one at a time and the house is twice as quiet. It is the more honest form and the lonelier, and your friend says afterward that he was glad of it, since he heard his own voice, and so did you.

choices.label: Hold the provincial's hands longer than the rubric says
choices.outcome: He lets you. It is a second and it is the thing you remember of the day, since it was a man and not a formula, and he says at the lunch that he could feel it and that it was right, and you are not sure what it was, and it was right.

events.title: The Deacon's Parish
events.body: Diaconate, and the province places its deacons in its own parishes, since the order has them, and yours is a parish across the city with a pastor who is a friar and famous for being difficult, {@prior} says, and famous for making deacons who can do anything, and the two are related. The first Sunday he has given you the baptisms, the eleven o'clock homily, and the parish council, and said that he will be at the golf course.

choices.label: Do all three, and do not telephone the golf course
choices.outcome: It is a bad Sunday and a good year. By Advent you can do anything, and he says so, in a letter to the formation director that the director shows you, and that says at the end that he would like you as his curate, which is a sentence the province reads.

choices.label: Do the baptisms and the homily and let the council meet without a deacon
choices.outcome: The council is offended and then, since it ran the parish for the difficult pastor for years, is not, and runs itself, and the pastor says the council did not need you, which was the test, and you had passed it by failing it.

choices.label: Telephone the golf course
choices.outcome: He answers on the ninth hole and says that a deacon who telephones is a deacon who will telephone as a pastor, and to do the three things, and that he will be back for the six o'clock, and is, and says the homily was too long, and it was.

events.title: The Deacon at the School
events.body: The province has put you in its high school for the diaconate year, since a deacon can teach and the school is short, and the school is four hundred boys, a lay principal, and six friars who are the last six, and the boys have not seen a young friar in a decade and do not know what to do with one. The first week a senior has asked, in class, why anyone would do this.

choices.label: Answer him, in front of the class, for the whole period
choices.outcome: It is a period and it is the best class you teach that year. Four of the boys ask for more and one of them enters the order at twenty-six and says it was the period, and the principal, who heard about it, says it was the first vocations talk the school has had that worked.

choices.label: Say you will tell him after class, and do
choices.outcome: He comes. It is an hour. He does not enter the order and is a good man and writes to you at Christmas for twenty years, and it was the hour and not the class, and you learn that the boys who ask after class are the ones.

choices.label: Say it is not the lesson, and teach the lesson
choices.outcome: The lesson is taught. The senior does not ask again and the class does not either, and the principal says at the end of the year that the boys respected you and did not know you, and that the school had hoped for the second thing, and you had not known it was on offer.

events.title: The Pastoral Year's Winter
events.body: The pastoral year is a deacon's year in a house that is not the studium, and the house is three old friars and a parish, and the student brothers are two hours away and the union is a memory, and it is February. The three old friars are kind and are old, and the parish is a parish, and you have said the Office alone for a month since the friars say it at a different hour, and the loneliness has a shape.

choices.label: Say the Office at their hour, whatever it costs the parish
choices.outcome: It costs the parish an hour a day and the parish does not notice, and the three old friars notice, and are moved, and one of them says at supper that the house has not had a fourth voice at Vespers in six years, and the winter is a different winter after that.

choices.label: Telephone the friend, every night
choices.outcome: He answers every night, since he has a winter too, and the two winters are one, and it is the friendship the order said would carry the life, carrying it, and the three old friars do not know, and the formation director does, and approves.

choices.label: Give the loneliness to the parish: be at everything
choices.outcome: The parish has never had a deacon at everything and is astonished and grateful and busy with you, and the loneliness is not gone and is used, and the pastor says at the end of the year that the parish will remember the deacon longer than the last three curates, and it does.

events.title: The Retreat Before Orders
events.body: The class goes to the province's retreat house, four of you now, for the week before ordination, and the retreat master is a friar who was on the mission for thirty years and preaches as if the retreat house were on the mountain. On the fourth day he takes each man alone and asks him one thing, and yours is this: who the three are, and whether they know.

choices.label: Name them, and say yes
choices.outcome: He says good, and that you should telephone each of them tonight and say so, since a man who is ordained without having said it is ordained alone, and you do, and two of them weep and one laughs, and all three are at the ordination, in the front, and know why.

choices.label: Name two, and say the third is not found
choices.outcome: He says the third is usually the one you have not noticed, and asks who sits beside you at supper, and you say, and he says that is the third, and it is, and you had not seen it, and see it for forty years.

choices.label: Say you are not sure they know
choices.outcome: He says that is the usual answer and the worst one, and that a friar is a man who has told his friends, and that the order is nothing else, and that you should fix it before Saturday, and you fix two of the three, and the third is fixed at the lunch, by him.

events.title: The Provincial's Letter
events.body: The letter comes in June, as they do, and it is the provincial's own hand, which he does for the newly ordained and for nobody else, and it names a house and a work, and the work is not the one you had hoped, and the house is one you have never seen, and the letter ends with a sentence that says the province has thought about it and that he would like you to trust that it has.

choices.label: Trust it, and write back one line
choices.outcome: The line is kept. The house is a good house and the work is the making of you, as the letter half said, and the provincial says at your jubilee that yours was the only reply he got that year that did not argue, and that he had noticed.

choices.label: Write back and ask, respectfully, why
choices.outcome: He answers in a page, which he did not have to, and the page is the province's reasoning and is sound and is not what you would have done, and you go, knowing why, and it is a little easier and a little harder both.

choices.label: Telephone the friend before answering
choices.outcome: The friend says to go, since it is the order, and to say so in one line, and to argue about it with him and not with the provincial, and you argue with him for an hour and write the one line, and it is the pattern for every letter after.

events.title: Ordination
events.body: The cathedral, since the bishop ordains, and the order in the front pews, and the family behind them, and the three, wherever they are sitting, and the prostration on the stone, which lasts longer than you had thought and is the part you remember: the litany going on above you, the names of the saints, the founder's among them, and the stone cold, and the thing being done to you while you lie still.

choices.label: Lie still, and let the litany be the thing
choices.outcome: It is the thing. You stand up a different man, or the same man with the thing done, and the bishop's hands are the seal and the stone was the prayer, and the old friar says afterward that he watched your back and it did not move, and that his had not either.

choices.label: Listen for the founder's name in the litany, and the three's saints
choices.outcome: You hear them all: the founder, and the three names, one after another, since you asked the master of ceremonies, and the three do not know until you tell them at the lunch, and it is the thing they remember of the day, which was the point.

choices.label: Think of the family behind the friars, and what it cost them
choices.outcome: Your mother is weeping and your father is not, and it cost them a son, in the way the novice director said, borrowed, and you get up from the stone and find them with your eyes before the friars, and the friars see it, and understand, since they had families too.

events.title: The First Mass
events.body: The first Mass is in the priory church where you were a pre-novice, since that is the custom, and the parish that watched a pre-novice work the pantry and the playground has come to see what it made, and the woman who ran the pantry is in the front row, and the pastor who was short of everyone is the deacon, and {@old_friar} is in the choir, and the homily is yours.

choices.label: Preach about the pantry, and the woman in the front row
choices.outcome: She weeps, which she has not done in public in twenty years, the pastor says, and the parish understands what the order is for, since it was in front of them, and the old friar says it was the first First Mass homily he has heard that was about somebody else.

choices.label: Preach about the order: what it is, and what it did with you
choices.outcome: The friars are moved and the parish is polite and the woman in the front row says at the lunch that it was a good homily and that she had not understood a word, and the old friar says that is the order's usual problem, and you hear it.

choices.label: Say three sentences, and let the Mass be the homily
choices.outcome: The Mass is the homily. The parish, which has heard forty First Mass homilies, is grateful, and the pastor says it was the first one he could have said the Canon after without a rest, and the woman in the front row says nothing and squeezes your hand at the door, hard.

events.title: The Old Friar's Funeral
events.body: {@old_friar} has died in the house during the year, in his sleep, at eighty-eight, and the house has done the things: the vigil in the choir, the friars taking turns through the night, the funeral with the provincial, and the burial in the order's plot, and it is the first friar's death you have been inside, and the house has asked the student brothers to take the two-to-four watch, and it is you and {@confrere}.

choices.label: Say the Office of the Dead over him, the whole of it
choices.outcome: It takes the two hours. The friend says it with you. It is the first time either of you has said it for a man you knew and it is not the last, and you say it for each other, in the end, one of you, and it began at two in the morning in a choir.

choices.label: Sit with him and tell each other what he said
choices.outcome: Two hours of his sentences, and the friend has ones you did not, and you have ones he did not, and the old man is more present in the choir than he was in the last year of his life, and the friars who come at four find the two of you laughing, and understand.

choices.label: Keep the silence; he kept it
choices.outcome: Two hours of it. It is the longest you have been silent with another man and it is not empty, and the friend says at four that it was the best conversation the two of you have had, and it was, and the old man would have said so.

events.title: The Bishop at the Union
events.body: The bishop of the diocese has come to the union, since the four orders' students are the diocese's neighbours and he would like to know them, and has sat with the Augustinians at lunch, since they were in the middle, and asked what the orders are for, in a diocese, in a sentence, and the Franciscans have said the poor and the Dominicans, at the next table, have said the truth, and it is your table's turn.

choices.label: Say: to show a diocese what a community looks like
choices.outcome: He is quiet and then says that is the best answer he has had from a religious in ten years, since it is the thing his priests do not have, and that he would like to visit the house, and does, and the priory has a bishop at supper twice a year after, which the province had not managed in forty.

choices.label: Say: to run the parishes the diocese cannot
choices.outcome: He says that is what the diocese thinks and had hoped the orders thought something else, and the Franciscans laugh, and it was the honest answer and the wrong one, and he does not visit, and the parishes are given, in time, since that is what the province is for, he thinks.

choices.label: Ask him what a diocese is for, in a sentence
choices.outcome: He laughs and answers, and it is a good answer, and the lunch is an hour longer than it was meant to be, and his secretary says afterward that he has not seen the bishop enjoy a lunch in a year, and the union has a bishop who likes it, which is worth a building.

events.title: The Restless Heart, First Time
events.body: It is the fourth year and it has come as the founder said it would: a restlessness that is not doubt and not desire and not tiredness and is all three, and that the formation director calls, when you tell him, the thing the order is named for, and that he says will come again, and that the men it does not come to are the ones who leave, oddly, since they have nothing to bring.

choices.label: Bring it to the chapel, every night, for a season
choices.outcome: The season is Lent and then Easter and it does not go and it changes, and by Pentecost it is a kind of prayer, and the formation director says the founder took nine years and you took one, and that it will come back, and you will know it, and you do.

choices.label: Work it off: the parish, the school, the union, everything
choices.outcome: It goes, or is buried, and the formation director says burying is a way, and that it comes back sooner when buried, and it does, in the first year of priesthood, larger, and you know it then, and bring it to the chapel that time.

choices.label: Tell the friend, and let him carry half
choices.outcome: He carries half. It is what the three are for, the director says, and the founder had Alypius, and the restlessness is a thing the two of you talk about for forty years, and it is the thread of the friendship, and neither of you would have it otherwise.

events.title: The Lutheran Seminary Comes to Lunch
events.body: The union shares a library with the Lutheran seminary across the road, and once a year the two have lunch, and this year the Lutheran students have asked for a session with the Augustinians in particular, since their founder was one, they say, and would like to know what the order thinks of him. The formation director has said it is your table's to answer and that the province would like it answered well.

choices.label: Say the order claims him: a friar who left, and the best-known one
choices.outcome: The Lutherans are delighted and the union's Dominicans are appalled and the formation director says it was the honest answer and the generous one and that the province will hear of it, and it does, and it is divided, and the Lutherans send a delegation to the priory at Christmas, with a cake.

choices.label: Say the order prays for him, as for every friar who left
choices.outcome: It is the traditional answer and the Lutherans hear it as it is meant, mostly, and the lunch is a good one and not a memorable one, and the union's Dominicans nod, and the formation director says it was safe and that safe was allowed.

choices.label: Ask them what he thought of the order
choices.outcome: They tell you, at length, and it is mixed, and it is the best hour of the year, since it is the order seen from outside by men who read, and the formation director says the question was better than any answer, and the lunches are two hours after that.

events.title: The Novice Director Writes
events.body: The novice director has written to you, in the sixth year, which he does not do, to say that the novitiate has a novice who is where you were in the ninth night, and that he would like you to come for a weekend and be, he says, a man who was there and stayed, since the novice will not hear it from him. It is the diaconate year and the weekend is the weekend of the parish's confirmations.

choices.label: Go; the parish can confirm without a deacon
choices.outcome: The pastor is annoyed and the novice is not, since a deacon came from two hours away to sit with him, and he stays, and is professed, and is a friar of the province, and the novice director says it was the weekend, and the pastor forgives you by Advent.

choices.label: Telephone the novice instead, that night
choices.outcome: It is an hour and it is not the same and it is something, and he stays, or does not on account of it, and the novice director says a telephone is a telephone, and does not write again, and you wonder for years.

choices.label: Go the weekend after
choices.outcome: The weekend after is too late, the novice director says, kindly, since the novice left on the Tuesday, and you learn that the order's timing is not the parish's, and it is a thing you know for the rest of your life and it cost a novice to learn.

events.title: The Four on the Steps
events.body: The photograph on the studium steps, the week before ordination: four of you, where there were six in the novitiate and nine in the pre-novitiate, and the formation director at one end and the prior at the other, and {@confrere} beside you, and the photographer has said to look at the camera, and you are counting the men who are not on the steps.

choices.label: Count them, and say their names under your breath
choices.outcome: Five names. The friend hears you and says them with you, and the photographer takes the picture in the middle of it, and it is the picture: four men saying five names, and it is on the wall of the studium for thirty years and nobody knows what they are saying.

choices.label: Look at the camera; the four are the class
choices.outcome: It is a good picture and a plain one. The five are not in it and are in you, and you write to two of them that week, and they write back, and the picture is on the wall and they are not, and that is what a picture is.

choices.label: Ask the director to say a word for the five before the shutter
choices.outcome: He says it, a sentence, and the four are quiet, and the shutter goes, and it is the photograph with four men not smiling, and the province wonders why, and the four know, and it is theirs.
